publishing.purpose: Credibility with a professional audience and branded search. The strongest of the ten for reaching decision-makers directly.
publishing.links: Links are usable and the audience is the right one, but treat reach, not SEO, as the return.
publishing.canonical: NO. LinkedIn articles support no canonical tag, so LinkedIn is treated as the original source.
publishing.rule: Never republish an article that already exists on your own site - you would be handing LinkedIn the credit for your own page. Write LinkedIn-first pieces, or post a short summary with a link to the site version.

publishing.purpose: Domain authority and distribution for educational articles. Good for being found by people already reading in your subject area.
publishing.links: Outbound links are nofollow, so they pass no direct link equity. The value is referral traffic and brand exposure.
publishing.canonical: YES. Use the story settings or the import tool to set the canonical to your original article.
publishing.rule: Publish on your own site first, wait for it to be indexed (allow roughly 2-10 days), then republish here with the canonical set back to your site.

publishing.purpose: Building an owned mailing list and earning referral traffic from other newsletters. This is an audience channel, not a search channel.
publishing.links: Links work normally, and the recommendation network between newsletters is the real growth mechanism.
publishing.canonical: NO. Substack does not let publishers set a canonical, so its version is treated as canonical to Substack.
publishing.rule: Because there is no canonical, either write newsletter-first content or link prominently to the full article on your site. Expect the traffic to come from subscribers, not from Google.

publishing.purpose: Intercepting people who are already searching your subject. Quora answers themselves rank in Google, which is the point.
publishing.links: All Quora links are nofollow. Judge this channel on qualified traffic and on the answers ranking, never on backlinks.
publishing.canonical: Not applicable - answers are original content, not republished articles.
publishing.rule: Answer the question fully before any link, and never put a link in the opening paragraphs. Name a Space for the subject rather than the brand; people follow topics, not vendors.

publishing.purpose: A branded educational blog with contextual links back to the main site.
publishing.links: Links behave normally, which makes this one of the few genuinely dofollow options on the list.
publishing.canonical: You control the content, so this can host originals rather than republished copies.
publishing.rule: CHECK THE COST FIRST: the free tier gives only a name.wordpress.com subdomain, 1GB storage, no plugins (so no SEO plugin) and shows adverts you neither control nor earn from. For a brand blog, budget for the entry paid tier or accept those limits in writing.

publishing.purpose: Supplementary and repurposed content. Google-owned and free, but carries little editorial weight.
publishing.canonical: You control the template, so a manual canonical link back to the original is possible.
publishing.rule: Use for repurposed content only, and always link to the original article. Do not spend original writing time here while ranks 1-5 are still under-served.

publishing.purpose: Short educational posts, infographics and brand citations.
publishing.links: Links behave normally but the audience overlap with a professional certification audience is thin.
publishing.rule: Short-form and visual only. Do not put long-form educational articles here.

publishing.purpose: Contributed articles across educational and professional topics; useful for reach and citations.
publishing.links: Links work, but every submission passes through moderation before it appears.
publishing.canonical: No canonical control, so avoid posting an exact copy of a page you want to rank.
publishing.rule: Rewrite rather than copy. Treat as an occasional reach channel, not a pillar.

publishing.purpose: Only for genuine technical writing about the AI coach, learning technology or platform engineering.
publishing.links: Links work, but the terms of service explicitly prohibit content posted primarily for promotion or for creating backlinks.
publishing.canonical: YES. DEV supports a canonical_url field.

publishing.purpose: Technical content about the learning platform and its AI features.
publishing.links: Links work; reach comes from tag feeds rather than search.
publishing.canonical: YES. Draft Settings has an 'Are you republishing?' field for the canonical URL.
publishing.rule: Technical write-ups only. Set the canonical on every republished piece, and reply in the comments - engagement is what surfaces posts in tag feeds.
